one_liner: Cloud-based customer service platform for ticketing, live chat, help center, and omnichannel support.
self_serve_evidence: API tokens are self-generated in Admin Center (Apps and integrations > APIs), and Zendesk explicitly offers trial/sponsored developer accounts for building integrations.
api_surface: Broad REST API (developer.zendesk.com/api-reference) covering Ticketing, Help Center, Chat, Talk, and more, with hundreds of documented endpoints; Basic Auth/API-token method is deprecated in favor of OAuth Bearer tokens.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist; Zendesk's own 'MCP client' feature lets Zendesk AI agents consume external MCP servers rather than exposing an official first-party MCP server for the Zendesk API itself.
notes: Legacy API-token+Basic-Auth method is deprecated (Zendesk pushing OAuth); sandbox environments and trial/sponsored dev accounts are available.

one_liner: AI-first customer messaging, chat, and helpdesk platform built around the Fin AI agent.
self_serve_evidence: An access token is issued automatically as soon as a developer creates an app in the Intercom Developer Hub, no approval needed for private-app/own-workspace access.
api_surface: Broad REST API (conversations, contacts, tickets, articles, etc.) plus a dedicated Fin Agent API and Canvas Kit for building in-app experiences.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Intercom/Fin MCP Server documented at developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp.
notes: OAuth required only when building a public app that accesses other workspaces' data; free trial available for new workspaces to obtain a dev app.

one_liner: Cloud helpdesk and ticketing software for customer support teams.
self_serve_evidence: API key is visible directly in the agent's Profile Settings in the support portal, with no approval step, and a free trial account can be created to obtain one.
api_surface: REST API (developer.freshdesk.com) covering tickets, contacts, agents, companies, forums, solutions, surveys, and groups.
existing_mcp_detail: Freshdesk shipped a native MCP integration as an Early Access Program feature; community server effytech/freshdesk_mcp also exists.
notes: Official MCP is still in Early Access Program (EAP), so may require enabling/opt-in; API key auth format is 'apikey:X'.

one_liner: Shared inbox / customer communication hub unifying email and omnichannel messages for support teams.
self_serve_evidence: API tokens are self-serve from account settings for single-workspace/internal use, but OAuth2 (required for public, multi-customer App Store integrations) needs Front's app framework and 'an exception' approval for non-OAuth public apps.
api_surface: Broad REST 'Core API' covering conversations, contacts, inboxes, rules, tags, and teams, with token scopes split across features/namespaces/permissions; also exposes an MCP server.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Front MCP server (beta) documented at dev.frontapp.com/docs/mcp-server.
blocker: Distributing a public/multi-tenant integration requires OAuth2 plus Front App Store review (or an explicit exception); single-workspace token access is unrestricted.
notes: MCP server access itself is one of the token 'features' that can be scoped/limited, suggesting fine-grained control for agent use cases.

one_liner: Modern B2B customer support platform (tickets, Slack/Teams-based support, shared Slack channels) built for SaaS companies.
self_serve_evidence: API tokens are generated directly from the Pylon dashboard settings page with no mention of approval or a required paid tier, and can be verified immediately via the /me endpoint.
api_surface: REST API (docs.usepylon.com) covering accounts, teams, issues, and more; documented breadth is moderate compared to older incumbents.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Pylon MCP server documented at docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/pylon-mcp.
notes: Authentication page itself is sparse on endpoint breadth details; full API reference exists separately.

one_liner: Help desk software combining ticketing, live chat, and call center features.
self_serve_evidence: API keys are self-generated in Configuration > System > API for existing accounts, but the number of allowed keys is gated by paid plan tier (1 key on Small Business up to 100 on Enterprise) and it's unclear if API access is enabled during the 30-day free trial.
api_surface: REST API (v3 current, v1 legacy) covering ticketing, chat, and call-center functionality; documented with filtering support.
existing_mcp_detail: Official LiveAgent MCP server from parent company QualityUnit (github.com/QualityUnit/liveagent-mcp-server).
blocker: API key quota/availability is tied to paid plan tier, and free-trial API access is unconfirmed.
notes: 30-day free trial advertised (no credit card), but pricing page shows API keys as a paid-plan line item rather than a trial feature.

one_liner: API-first, GraphQL-native customer support tool built for software/B2B companies.
self_serve_evidence: A developer can create a Machine User and API key directly from Settings in the Plain dashboard with selectable permissions, with no sales/approval step documented.
api_surface: Single GraphQL API (core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1) that Plain says has 'no limitations in what can be done via the API vs the UI', i.e. very broad coverage of the product.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Plain MCP server announced at plain.com/blog/mcp-server and plain.com/changelog/plain-mcp.
notes: GraphQL-only API (no separate REST surface); pricing/free-tier details weren't confirmed on the docs pages fetched, only self-serve key creation.

one_liner: Help desk and shared-inbox software for customer support teams.
self_serve_evidence: Developers create an OAuth2 app themselves via Profile > My Apps > 'Create My App' with no approval process mentioned, and a free trial account is available to sign up.
api_surface: Broad REST Mailbox API (conversations, customers, inboxes, attachments, custom fields, tags, reports, webhooks, workflows, teams) plus a separate Docs API.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Help Scout MCP server (beta) at mcp-beta.helpscout.net.
notes: OAuth2-only (no plain API key/basic auth); both Authorization Code and Client Credentials flows supported; credentials must be tied to an active invited user.

one_liner: Ecommerce-focused helpdesk/customer support platform with deep Shopify/BigCommerce integration.
self_serve_evidence: Private-app API key auth (email + API key) is self-serve and testable directly in the API docs, while OAuth2 is reserved for public/delegated apps which typically require Gorgias partner/app-review approval.
api_surface: REST API (developers.gorgias.com) covering tickets, customers, integrations, and ecommerce-context resources; interactive docs allow live testing.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Gorgias MCP server in Open Beta.
notes: Public/multi-tenant OAuth2 apps likely require Gorgias app-store review, adding friction beyond basic private-app API key use.

one_liner: AI-native, enterprise customer service platform organized around a single lifelong customer conversation/timeline.
self_serve_evidence: API access requires being an existing paying Gladly customer with an admin who grants a user the 'API User' permission to generate tokens; there is no public self-serve signup, published pricing, or free trial found.
api_surface: Broad REST API (developer.gladly.com/rest) covering customer profiles, conversations/timeline, comms (SMS/email), knowledge/answers, agents, inboxes, business hours, analytics/exports, tasks, and webhooks, plus a separate sandbox domain and an App Platform (appcfg CLI) for config-based apps.
existing_mcp_detail: No official Gladly MCP server found; only third-party integration/connector listings surfaced.
blocker: No public self-serve trial or pricing — a developer must already be a contracted Gladly customer (enterprise sales) and get admin-granted API User permission before any credentials can be issued.
notes: Docs reference a QA/sandbox environment, but both still presuppose an existing organization domain, i.e. an existing paid account.
